title: Legacy CRM Admin Console — Permission Architecture and Module Management
summary: The administrative console architecture for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering the tile-based module management interface, tiered permission model with five permission set categories, external application integration via Connected Apps, and read-only access patterns for home office users.

findings.admin_console_architecture: The Admin Console is a centralized configuration hub accessible as a tab within the CRM application. It presents a tile-based interface where each tile maps to a functional module: Account Management, Activity History Administration, Address Administration, Call Administration, Call Plan, CLM, Config Service, Dynamic Lists, License Administration, Meetings, MIRF Administration, Mobile, Monitoring, Orders, Products, Quick Action Administration, Ratings, Reports and Dashboards. Each tile links to the module-specific configuration pages. The Admin Console tab can be hidden on mobile by setting Custom Tab Settings to Default Off for the relevant profile.
findings.tiered_permission_model: Five permission set categories control access to Admin Console features: (1) Admin Console All — provides full CRUD and administrative capabilities across all tiles. (2) Basic Admin Permissions — covers foundational administration: Address Administration, Account Management, Planner, Customer Merge Settings, License (DEA and SDL) Setup, Monitoring, SBC Config Setup, SBC Field Mapping, Search Before Create, State License Number Administration, Synchronization, and Trigger Handler. (3) Advanced Admin Permissions — adds higher-privilege capabilities: Ada-Lite, AdaLite Provisioning, Application Settings, Mobile, Quick and Custom Action Administration, Ratings, and Reports and Dashboards. (4) Basic Business Admin Permissions — covers product and territory operations: Product Restrictions Jobs, Products, Samples Management, Samples Management Config, and Territories. (5) Advanced Business Admin Permissions — adds planning and execution administration: Activity History Administration, Activity Plan, Activity Plan Config, Activity Plan Settings, Call Administration, Call Plan, Call Plan Config, Email, Meetings, MIRF Administration, Opt Administration, Order Administration, Orders, Signature Audit, and Store Management. CLM Admin Permissions is a separate category providing CLM-specific access.
findings.permission_set_cloning_constraint: Managed package permission sets cannot be modified directly — administrators must clone them to customize access. However, cloned permission sets do not receive automatic updates when the managed package is upgraded. Administrators with profiles cloned from the platform admin profile with listed permission sets assigned will lose permissions to all tiles after an upgrade and must manually reassign.
findings.external_application_integration: External applications can be surfaced as tiles within the Admin Console through Connected App configuration. The integration requires: (1) creating a Connected App with OAuth enabled (Full access and refresh_token/offline_access scopes), (2) activating Canvas App Settings with a Signed Request POST access method and Lightning Component/Visualforce page locations, (3) pre-authorizing users via the permission set, and (4) setting the OAuth policy to Admin approved users are pre-authorized. This enables third-party tools (content adaptation services, detailing customization platforms) to appear seamlessly alongside native admin modules.
findings.read_only_access_for_home_office: CLM and Product tiles support a read-only access mode for home office users. Read-only CLM access exposes Sequences, Presentations, and Settings tabs for browsing without modification. Read-only Product access exposes Product Hierarchy and Product Alignment tabs. Configuration requires the dedicated read-only permission set plus Read access to IsCustom fields on Presentation objects and Is Active fields on Product Message objects. If full CRUD permissions exist on Presentations, Sequences, and Products, the Admin Console displays modification buttons regardless of the read-only permission set.

title: Legacy CRM Dynamic UI Renderer — Metadata-Driven Mobile Layout Architecture
summary: The metadata-driven Dynamic UI rendering architecture for mobile CRM, covering server-configured layout rendering, field support capabilities, global variable resolution, formula field limitations on mobile, and configurable menu tab navigation with icon customization.

findings.metadata_driven_rendering: The mobile application uses a Dynamic UI renderer that constructs page layouts from server-side metadata configuration rather than hard-coded native views. Administrators configure which fields, sections, and related lists appear on each record type's mobile layout through the platform's standard page layout editor. The renderer interprets this metadata at runtime to build the native mobile interface, supporting both Comfy (spacious) and Compact (dense) display density settings.
findings.field_support_capabilities: The renderer supports field default values (pre-populated on record creation), validation rules (enforced client-side before save), dependent picklists (cascading field value filtering), and lookup filters (restricting related record selection). Lookup filter support excludes the includes, excludes, and within operators. Dependent picklist chains can extend multiple levels deep with the mobile app resolving the full dependency tree from metadata.
findings.global_variable_resolution: Five categories of global variables are available in the mobile context: $Label (custom label values), $Organization (organization-level settings), $Profile (current user profile attributes), $Setup (hierarchical custom settings), and $User (current user record fields). These variables are resolved at runtime against locally cached metadata, enabling dynamic behavior without network round-trips.
findings.formula_field_limitations: Formula fields on mobile are limited to Checkbox and Text return types. The same formula function exclusion list applies as for email templates: functions requiring server-side evaluation (CURRENCYRATE, DISTANCE, GETRECORDIDS, GETSESSIONID, HYPERLINK, INCLUDE, ISCLONE, VLOOKUP, and others) are not supported in the mobile rendering context. Formula fields with unsupported return types or functions display their raw stored values or blank.
findings.menu_tab_navigation: Configurable menu tabs define the primary navigation structure of the mobile application. Each tab can display a custom icon sourced from a Unicode icon mapping table configured through Custom Metadata Types (Navigation Icons). The icon configuration maps a metadata record name to a Unicode character code, enabling administrators to customize the navigation appearance without code changes. Lightning Web Components can also be surfaced as tabs alongside standard object tabs.

title: Legacy CRM Deep Linking — URI-Based Navigation and Cross-Application Integration
summary: The deep linking architecture for a legacy life sciences CRM mobile application, enabling URI-scheme-based navigation to specific records, views, and actions from external systems, push notifications, and within the application itself.

findings.deep_link_uri_scheme: The application registers a custom URI scheme that enables direct navigation to specific screens and records. Deep links follow the pattern: scheme://deeplink/navigation-target/parameters. Supported navigation targets include: record detail views (by record ID), list views (by object type and filter criteria), modal dialogs (for record creation or action execution), and custom web views (for external content display within the app shell).
findings.cross_application_integration: Deep links enable integration with external systems: push notifications can include deep link URIs that navigate users directly to relevant records when tapped, email templates can embed deep links for one-tap navigation from compliant emails to specific CRM screens, and third-party applications (MDM portals, compliance systems) can construct deep links to hand off context to the CRM application.
findings.feedback_deep_link_pattern: A representative example of the deep link architecture: the user feedback capture system uses a deep link to open a modal dialog for the Feedback custom object with a new record action. The URI includes a source parameter (URL-encoded, max 255 characters) that is persisted to the Source field on the created record, enabling the system to track which screen or context triggered the feedback. This pattern — modal + sobject + action + context parameters — is reusable across custom objects and actions.
findings.notification_integration: Deep links can be embedded in app notifications through the notification management system. When a notification fires, its associated deep link determines where the user navigates upon interaction. This creates a complete workflow: server-side event triggers notification, notification displays in the device notification center, user interaction navigates directly to the relevant CRM context without manual search or navigation.
